scenario: Open a valid exact bundle/version deep link.
expected: Heading, baseline, coverage, systems requests, and export selection retain the same validated pair.

scenario: Open an absent bundle or a version belonging to another bundle.
expected: Return an explicit unavailable/invalid selection; do not substitute the first bundle or current version.

scenario: Switch between a published version and a draft with different metadata.
expected: Header and body refer to the selected version; lineage-level metadata is labeled separately.

scenario: Open a direct-policy finding from a POA&M with no bundle candidates.
expected: No panic occurs; the user reaches direct-policy evidence or an explicit supported alternative.

scenario: Open a policy finding with more than one bundle context.
expected: Use a validated retained pair or a context picker; do not combine unrelated bundle and version arrays.

scenario: Move between evidence controls with keyboard navigation, then use Back.
expected: Visible control, URL, selected observation, and restored focus remain coherent.

scenario: Open the same exact-CVE plan from Systems, fleet CVEs, and a direct Compliance URL.
expected: Each caller shows the same plan revision and family; Evidence navigation is available and correctly bound.

scenario: Open current, link-baseline, and closure evidence from a completed plan.
expected: Each mode preserves its own source identity and time; historical links never silently open current evidence.

scenario: Provide an assessment with the complete digest only, then with the enforced digest only.
expected: Matrix, detail, verifier, and export implement the approved compatibility rule and identify any display-only difference.

scenario: Provide matching policy versions but different per-host effective overrides.
expected: Each host is evaluated against its own effective configuration; cached metadata cannot substitute another host configuration.

scenario: Provide a newer evaluation attempt for an undeployed target.
expected: It cannot become an authoritative current result or authorize remediation/closure for the running target.

scenario: Split successful rule rows across separate evaluation attempts.
expected: No complete passing observation is synthesized from incompatible attempts.

scenario: Omit a required rule while all present rules pass.
expected: Completeness is partial/unavailable, not Pass; mutation capabilities follow the authoritative result.

scenario: Record a valid current report followed by a newer empty or invalid report.
expected: All current resolvers follow the approved newest-report rule; any last-known display is explicitly secondary.

scenario: Provide an exact legacy Nix result for one policy version and a different result for its lineage head.
expected: The selected version is not replaced by the lineage head; the typed observation identity remains intact.

scenario: Provide completed CVE threshold counters without schema-1 exact occurrence evidence.
expected: Policy threshold status and exact-CVE finding authority remain distinct; no exact occurrence is fabricated.

scenario: Complete a clean exact scan after an older vulnerable scan.
expected: The current resolver honors the complete clean scan and does not fall back to old findings.

scenario: Read evidence and rollups before and after first-time finding-identity materialization.
expected: The apparent technical finding population is stable, or a documented reconciliation state explains the difference.

scenario: Use a baseline with full, partial, unmapped, and recovery-required requirements.
expected: The denominator includes every selected requirement; the four coverage counts sum to that denominator.

scenario: Map several policies to one requirement and one policy to several requirements.
expected: Requirement coverage, policy control counts, and plan counts remain separate units.

scenario: Create an error-only host and a never-evaluated host.
expected: Neither enters an unqualified clean collection or clean export.

scenario: Use only waived controls on an evaluated host.
expected: Technical score, waiver count, and accepted-compliance label follow the explicitly approved formula.

scenario: Link multiple findings to one plan and show one finding under multiple bundle contexts.
expected: Plans, findings, and distinct systems are not summed interchangeably or double-counted.

scenario: Load a plan containing only exact-CVE findings.
expected: Its compact row uses the exact-CVE count and family label, not zero policy findings.

scenario: Give a non-Admin access to one of two environments and query every summary/detail route.
expected: Unauthorized host identities and counts are excluded before aggregation; hidden details stay non-enumerable.

scenario: Filter by environment, result, bundle revision, and finding-family scope.
expected: Rows and aggregates declare and use the same scope; empty access is not interpreted as fleet access.

scenario: Create from the same current failed policy finding through Systems and Compliance.
expected: Stable finding identity and server-owned authority checks are identical; the finding remains Fail after creation.

scenario: Attempt creation from Pass, stale, partial, or an unrelated observation.
expected: The server rejects the action without creating a plan, reference, or active link.

scenario: Create and link with a supported legacy observation-only policy context.
expected: All supported entry points preserve the typed observation instead of requiring a fabricated assessment ID.

scenario: Browse more than 50 compatible plans/findings.
expected: Continuation reaches every allowed candidate; a first-page limit is not presented as the complete set.

scenario: Choose a 14-day target with default policy milestones enabled.
expected: Milestone dates obey the approved target-date rule or the UI reports an explicit schedule conflict.

scenario: Commit generic creation, then fail response-detail loading or lose the response.
expected: The client can reconcile the committed plan and revision; retries do not claim a rollback or silently duplicate ownership.

scenario: Open policy-only, CVE-only, and direct-policy plans at the Compliance route.
expected: The tray works without unrelated catalog selection and shows only the correct family capabilities.

scenario: Open the exact-CVE Evidence action from the Compliance-hosted tray.
expected: A real callback leads to the canonical pair and intended target/observation.

scenario: Verify each non-completed lifecycle state.
expected: Verify is offered only when supported; the server still rejects invalid state transitions.

scenario: Edit plan text locally, then run Verify.
expected: Successful verification updates saved attempt/revision without discarding unrelated unsaved text.

scenario: Trigger stale-revision, unauthorized, and deleted/hidden-record errors during edit.
expected: The UI preserves recoverable drafts, distinguishes unavailable state, and never claims an unsaved change persisted.

scenario: Retire policy and exact-CVE links, then close and reopen related plans.
expected: Both families expose accurate active, retired, and closure-set history without treating all retirement as closure.

scenario: Change or remove an assignee identity after the plan was created.
expected: Historical identity remains readable; unavailable identity is not a valid new assignment and does not confer access.

scenario: Mutate a plan while a history continuation is in flight.
expected: Pages do not combine incompatible record revisions; restart behavior is explicit and does not duplicate rows.

scenario: Verify while a linked finding still fails.
expected: Persist a rejected sealed attempt and new revision; retain awaiting-verification status and active links.

scenario: Close while current evidence fails.
expected: Return the documented 412 with the committed attempt/revision; the client adopts that revision.

scenario: Show a passing verification, then publish newer failed evidence before Close.
expected: Close re-resolves current authority under locks and rejects stale readiness.

scenario: Complete all milestones while one current finding still fails.
expected: Milestone completion does not authorize closure.

scenario: Approve a policy waiver for the exact current failed observation.
expected: Only an applicable unexpired waiver under the approved policy rule can satisfy closure; original Fail remains visible.

scenario: Expire or change the observation underlying an accepted policy waiver.
expected: The old waiver cannot satisfy the new closure attempt.

scenario: Create an exact-CVE link on A, deploy fixed B, and scan B clean.
expected: Record the present MISSING behavior as a regression baseline; implement a different expectation only after the continuity decision.

scenario: Keep deployment A and provide a strictly newer complete schema-1 scan with pair absence.
expected: Exact-CVE verification can return Pass without changing the immutable link baseline.

scenario: Keep the pair present but whitelist it, justify it, or accept its risk.
expected: None of those states becomes exact absence or silently satisfies the current exact-CVE Pass requirement.

scenario: Race closure/reopen against ownership changes, environment moves, and link replacement.
expected: Re-resolve access and exact subjects; preserve one active owner and immutable closure history, or return a typed conflict.

scenario: Request and decide a policy waiver through its user-visible entry point.
expected: The complete role-separated workflow exists; accepted-risk triage is not used as a substitute.

scenario: Attach an immutable assignment-version reference, then update that assignment.
expected: The reference stays on its original version; current assignment state and its effect are separate.

scenario: Update assignment reason with omitted, null, and nonempty values.
expected: Omitted preserves, null clears, and a value replaces under the expected-version precondition.

scenario: Use Viewer or Operator credentials on Admin-only assignment maintenance.
expected: UI capabilities match the restriction; forged requests are rejected without mutation.

scenario: Use missing or mismatched CSRF tokens on every basic bundle and assignment write route.
expected: Each state-changing route rejects the request according to the common CSRF contract.

scenario: Save bundle edits while requirement hydration is delayed or fails.
expected: The UI cannot replace an unknown prior requirement selection with an empty one; real persisted membership is preserved.

scenario: Select two bundles with disjoint host and control data.
expected: Downloaded bytes contain the complete selected set, not just the bundle active before the modal opened.

scenario: Deselect the original bundle and retain another bundle.
expected: No original-bundle data appears; the retained selection controls both filename and contents.

scenario: Export two revisions with different selected policies and metadata.
expected: Each request and record retains the chosen immutable version; no current-pointer substitution occurs.

scenario: Restrict export to one authorized environment.
expected: All host/control rows and totals use that scope; hidden environments cannot appear in metadata or totals.

scenario: Export the clean host scope with error, unscanned, waiver-only, and passing fixtures.
expected: Membership follows the approved clean/completeness rule and does not hide unknown states.

scenario: Toggle inclusion of waivers and source evidence.
expected: Each format implements the declared toggle semantics, with explicit source omissions and coherent totals.

scenario: Export native JSON for an exact selected observation.
expected: Version, observation, authority, target, completeness, and relevant time identities survive, or the format is explicitly a summary.

scenario: Export multiple control rows for one host to CSV.
expected: Repeated rollup cells are not represented as additive distinct-host counts; quoting and row structure are validated.

scenario: Export with no authoritative classification or sensitivity metadata.
expected: Do not assert UNCLASSIFIED or low sensitivity by default; retain unspecified or validated user input.

scenario: Export old observations now, including absent and partial evidence.
expected: Export time is distinct from collection/evaluation time; no not-checked row is reported as an executed automated assessment.

scenario: Validate SARIF and OSCAL against pinned schemas and application semantics.
expected: Check every status, including not-checked, referenced resources, identifiers, and real waiver provenance; schema success alone is insufficient.

scenario: Fail a middle evidence request or change evidence midway through a large export.
expected: No apparently complete partial report is emitted; changed-snapshot, cancellation, and overflow behavior are explicit.

scenario: Delay a POA&M list for bundle A, then switch to bundle B.
expected: The late A response cannot replace B rows or counts; obsolete assignment scope is cleared.

scenario: Delay two assignment previews or policy-detail reads in opposite order.
expected: Each response applies only to its original immutable scope and newest request generation.

scenario: Fail requirement coverage, then retry the same selection.
expected: Retry issues a new request and can succeed without changing bundle selection.

scenario: Keep initial evidence loading indefinitely, then dismiss it.
expected: Close and Escape remain usable; no background response reopens the dismissed drawer.

scenario: Create, link, update, verify, and close while adjacent views remain mounted.
expected: Every affected relationship/list/rollup is refreshed or marked stale; unrelated drafts and inactive views are not needlessly reset.

scenario: Restore an import draft after logout/account change or with a different source file.
expected: Draft ownership and source validation are explicit; restored browser state cannot approve or import unreviewed content.

scenario: Compare populated page and bundle drawer with the reference.
expected: Explicitly account for section order, requirement coverage, remediation strip, systems filters, and missing columns.

scenario: Compare complete, partial, missing, and failed evidence drawers.
expected: Result, completeness, source type, identity, observation time, and action authority remain distinguishable.

scenario: Compare policy and exact-CVE create/link/detail surfaces.
expected: Family-specific context, assignee, due date, plan, findings, verification, history, and unavailable actions retain clear hierarchy.

scenario: Use nested dialogs by keyboard in both themes.
expected: Initial focus, wrapping, Escape precedence, and return focus work without closing or reopening the wrong layer.

scenario: Use narrow desktop and mobile with long package, policy, requirement, and assignee text.
expected: Important metadata/actions remain reachable; no hidden overflow or collapsed concept is accepted without a recorded decision.

scenario: Inspect export/import/assignment pending, error, empty, and read-only states.
expected: Controls match capabilities; incomplete hydration, export scope, and retry guidance remain visible and truthful.
